raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

Add native `qhead_per_kv_head=96`, `head_dim=576` support to DeepSeek sparse-attention target recompute on SM90 and the SM100 architecture family.

- SM90 uses two H48 head tiles, restricted to the sparse-attention target path. Existing sparse-indexer and dense score-recompute dispatch remains unchanged.
- SM100-family dispatch uses `(M, N, K) = (96, 128, 192)`.
- Add L0 reference tests with and without `topk_length`, including empty and partial rows.
- Add L1 production-boundary tests for logical top-k 2048, 2049, 2050, and 2051.

## Why

H96 callers currently pad Q/LSE to H128 before target recompute. This performs 33.3% more head work and adds caller-side padding traffic and launch overhead.

The native layouts remove that work without introducing a public API change or tensor-layout conversion.

The tile configurations were selected through compile/run validation and profiling:

- On SM90, H48 × 2 consistently outperformed the padded H128 kernel. An H64 × 2 masked alternative showed no stable performance gain and would add masking complexity.
- On the SM100 architecture family, the N64 attention epilogue cannot represent H96 because it would require an unsupported TMEM repetition. N128 covers all 96 heads using the existing fixed repetition.
- K192 keeps the SM100 kernel within the shared-memory budget while retaining two KV pipeline stages. It was 1.81x faster than K64 at top-k 2048 and 1.88x faster at top-k 2051 on SM103.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

- No public API or signature changes.
- Extends sparse-attention target recompute to accept native H96/D576 on SM90 and the SM100 architecture family.
- SM90 sparse-indexer and dense score-recompute behavior remains unchanged.
- Native H96 agrees with the padded-H128 implementation to a maximum absolute error of `3.50e-10` and a maximum relative L2 error of `1.33e-7` across the production performance cases.

## Testing

### GPU correctness tests

Test environment:

- cuDNN Frontend source: `1.32.0`
- CuTe DSL: `4.8.0`, compiling with CUDA 13.4
- PyTorch CUDA version: 13.0

```bash
# SM90, cuDNN backend 9.15.1
python -m pytest -q \
  deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_sparse_score_recompute.py \
  -k "h96_native" -m "L0 or L1"
# 6 passed, 1 warning

python -m pytest -q \
  deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_sparse_score_recompute.py
# 16 passed, 6 skipped, 4 xfailed, 1 warning
```

```bash
# SM103, cuDNN backend 9.20.0
python -m pytest -q \
  deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_sparse_score_recompute.py \
  -k "h96_native" -m "L0 or L1"
# 6 passed

python -m pytest -q \
  deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_sparse_score_recompute.py
# 26 passed
```

## Performance

Benchmark shape:

- BF16
- `B=1`
- `SQ=4096`
- `SKV=32768`
- `H=96`
- `D=576`
- 20 launches per sample
- 7 alternating rounds
- CUDA-event timing
- Median reported

The non-CSA case passes `topk_length=None`. CSA top-k 2049–2051 uses physical top-k 2176 and `topk_length`; CSA top-k 2048 uses physical top-k 2048.

Speedup is H128 latency divided by native-H96 latency, so higher is better.

| SM | Mode | Logical top-k | Native H96 | H128 kernel | Kernel speedup | H128 adapter E2E | E2E speedup |
|---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 90 | no CSA | 2048 | 3.152 ms | 3.335 ms | 1.058x | 4.022 ms | 1.276x |
| 90 | CSA | 2048 | 3.209 ms | 3.370 ms | 1.050x | 4.032 ms | 1.257x |
| 90 | CSA | 2049 | 3.224 ms | 3.401 ms | 1.055x | 4.081 ms | 1.266x |
| 90 | CSA | 2050 | 3.273 ms | 3.415 ms | 1.043x | 4.097 ms | 1.252x |
| 90 | CSA | 2051 | 3.261 ms | 3.450 ms | 1.058x | 4.114 ms | 1.262x |
| 103 | no CSA | 2048 | 1.023 ms | 1.822 ms | 1.781x | 2.504 ms | 2.448x |
| 103 | CSA | 2048 | 1.024 ms | 1.523 ms | 1.487x | 2.196 ms | 2.144x |
| 103 | CSA | 2049 | 1.410 ms | 2.242 ms | 1.589x | 2.921 ms | 2.071x |
| 103 | CSA | 2050 | 1.406 ms | 2.247 ms | 1.598x | 2.919 ms | 2.076x |
| 103 | CSA | 2051 | 1.404 ms | 2.241 ms | 1.596x | 2.921 ms | 2.080x |

Reverse kernel-compilation-order runs retained positive speedups in every case:

- No-CSA top-k 2048: 1.058x on SM90 and 1.770–1.781x on SM103.
- CSA top-k 2048–2051, taking the lower result from either order: 1.043–1.058x on SM90 and 1.487–1.553x on SM103.

files.patch:
@@ -594,6 +594,14 @@ def _dispatch_sparse_attn_tile_params(
     """
     m = qhead_per_kv_head
 
+    # H96 cannot use the default n64 attention epilogue: Ld16x64bOp would
+    # require Repetition(96 // 2), but 48 is not a supported TMEM repetition.
+    # The existing n128 epilogue uses its fixed Repetition(8) load and covers
+    # all 96 heads natively.  Split D576 into three K192 chunks to retain two
+    # KV pipeline stages within the SM100 shared-memory budget.
+    if head_dim == 576 and qhead_per_kv_head == 96:
+        return m, 128, 192
+
     if compact:
         # --- Compact tuned configs ---
         # hd=512

@@ -132,7 +132,14 @@ def _sparse_score_recompute(
     assert num_head > num_head_kv and num_head % num_head_kv == 0, f"MQA required: num_head={num_head}, num_head_kv={num_head_kv}"
     qhead_per_kvhead = num_head // num_head_kv
 
-    tile_m, num_head_tiles = _compute_tile_m(qhead_per_kvhead)
+    if not is_index_scores and qhead_per_kvhead == 96:
+        # H96 is not divisible by the usual H64 tile. H48 x 2 preserves
+        # complete head coverage and is faster than externally padding the
+        # attention Q/LSE inputs to H128. Keep this target-only specialization
+        # out of the indexer and dense score-recompute paths.
+        tile_m, num_head_tiles = 48, 2
+    else:
+        tile_m, num_head_tiles = _compute_tile_m(qhead_per_kvhead)
 
     _require_int32_contiguous(topk_indices, "topk_indices")
     topk_max = topk_indices.shape[-1]

@@ -75,6 +75,73 @@ def test_sparse_attn_sm100_tiles_match_reference(num_heads, head_dim, topk, has_
     check_ref_sparse_score_recompute("attention", q, lse, local_ids, actual, aux=k, softmax_scale=scale, topk_length=lengths)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.L0
+@torch_fork_set_rng(seed=96)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_topk_length", [False, True])
+def test_sparse_attn_h96_native_matches_reference(has_topk_length):
+    """H96 uses native head tiles on both SM90 and the SM100 architecture family."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] not in (9, 10):
+        pytest.skip("native H96 sparse attention score recompute requires SM90 or SM100 family")
+    from cudnn import DSA
+
+    cfg = {"b": 1, "s_q": 4, "s_kv": 256, "head_dim": 576, "qhead_per_kv_head": 96, "topk": 128}
+    q, k, lse, local_ids, _ = _allocate(cfg, "attention", has_topk_length=False)
+    lengths = None
+    if has_topk_length:
+        lengths = torch.tensor([[0, 1, 127, 128]], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        positions = torch.arange(cfg["topk"], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).view(1, 1, -1)
+        local_ids.masked_fill_(positions >= lengths.unsqueeze(-1), -1)
+    else:
+        local_ids[..., -37:] = -1
+
+    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(cfg["head_dim"])
+    actual = DSA.sparse_attn_score_recompute_wrapper(
+        q,
+        k,
+        lse,
+        local_ids,
+        scale,
+        qhead_per_kv_head=cfg["qhead_per_kv_head"],
+        topk_length=lengths,
+        topk_indices_global=False,
+    )["target"]
+    check_ref_sparse_score_recompute("attention", q, lse, local_ids, actual, aux=k, softmax_scale=scale, topk_length=lengths)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L1
+@torch_fork_set_rng(seed=2051)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("logical_topk", [2048, 2049, 2050, 2051])
+def test_sparse_attn_h96_native_production_topk(logical_topk):
+    """Production top-k boundaries retain empty-row and invalid-suffix semantics."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] not in (9, 10):
+        pytest.skip("native H96 sparse attention score recompute requires SM90 or SM100 family")
+    from cudnn import DSA
+
+    heads, head_dim = 96, 576
+    physical_topk = math.ceil(logical_topk / 128) * 128
+    q = torch.zeros((1, 2, heads, head_dim), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    k = torch.zeros((1, physical_topk, head_dim), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    lse = torch.zeros((1, 2, heads), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.arange(physical_topk, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").view(1, 1, -1).expand(1, 2, -1).clone()
+    lengths = torch.tensor([[0, logical_topk]], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    positions = torch.arange(physical_topk, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").view(1, 1, -1)
+    indices.masked_fill_(positions >= lengths.unsqueeze(-1), -1)
+
+    actual = DSA.sparse_attn_score_recompute_wrapper(
+        q,
+        k,
+        lse,
+        indices,
+        1.0 / math.sqrt(head_dim),
+        qhead_per_kv_head=heads,
+        topk_length=lengths,
+        topk_indices_global=False,
+    )["target"]
+    expected = torch.zeros_like(actual)
+    expected[0, 1, :logical_topk] = 1.0 / logical_topk
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=1e-7, rtol=1e-4)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.L0
 @torch_fork_set_rng(seed=0)
 @with_dsa_sparse_score_recompute_params
